pick.title: Private Fusion Startup Fuse Energy Sets Record Neutron Yield With Dense Plasma Focus Device
pick.score: n/a — Frontier Saturday editorial slot (owner directive 2026-08-12); scorer has no frontier lane yet

evidence.summary: Fuse Energy Technologies' megajoule-class dense plasma focus device FAETON-X produced a peak yield of 1.27 trillion (1.27x10^12) neutrons in a single deuterium-deuterium shot, which the company says is the first publicly documented neutron yield at that level by any private fusion company. The device reportedly delivered about 40% more neutrons per megajoule than Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory's MJOLNIR facility, operating at 65 kV with roughly 1 MJ of stored energy and a record current efficiency of 4.5 MA/MJ.

primary_source.name: Research Square preprint: "Exceeding 10^12 D-D flash neutrons in the 4.5-MA 1-MJ dense plasma focus FAETON-X"

evidence.outlet: The Fusion Report (Substack, weekly fusion-industry roundup)

pick.why_strong: A private company publicly claiming to match or beat national-lab-class neutron yields is a genuine technical milestone that supports real synthesis — explaining dense-plasma-focus physics, how it differs from tokamak/laser fusion, and what neutron-yield thresholds actually mean for near-term revenue (radiation-effects testing) versus the longer path to net energy.
